leads.summary: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company behind Next.js, v0 and the AI SDK, selling deployment, sandboxes, AI gateway and observability for apps and agents. This posting is for a backend-leaning software engineer building user, group and membership management services.
leads.hook: The posting says the team builds user, group and membership management on JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js and AWS, with a security and reliability bar.
leads.angle_reason: MedVault's JWT auth with refresh-token rotation and per-user isolation at the queryset level maps directly to the user, group and membership work this role describes.

leads.summary: ParadeDB builds a Postgres extension that adds full-text, vector and aggregate search as a native index, so teams can avoid running a separate search system like Elasticsearch. It sells to developers and infrastructure teams who already run Postgres.
leads.hook: The homepage benchmark says ParadeDB text search runs 119x faster than vanilla Postgres at P95 on the 28M-row Hacker News dataset.
leads.angle_reason: Canopy's PostgreSQL-backed cache and multi-language static analysis are close to the indexing and query work of a Postgres-native developer tool.

leads.summary: Speedy Labs sells AI agents that reconcile rebate statements and payments for food-service distributors, manufacturers and buying groups, and write true net cost back to the ERP.
leads.hook: The site says every agent answer opens to the source statement lines behind it, with a short-paid Smithfield bacon line recovered as $1,240.
leads.angle_reason: MedVault turns uploaded documents into structured, schema-constrained AI output through a Gemini pipeline, close to reading statements and contracts for reconciliation.

leads.summary: Glass builds clinical AI for clinicians, covering clinical decision support, ambient scribing and patient guidance, grounded in peer-reviewed medical literature and drug information.
leads.hook: The site says every Glass response is grounded in peer-reviewed citations, with 40M+ PubMed citations behind the clinical agent.
leads.angle_reason: MedVault is a health-tech LLM pipeline with safety rules that forbid diagnosis or prescription, which is close to a clinical reasoning product.

leads.summary: Osium AI sells AI software that predicts materials and chemicals properties and supports R&D from formulation through scale-up for manufacturers.
leads.hook: The site claims property predictions for any material or chemical in a few seconds, covering formulation through scale-up.
leads.angle_reason: Both are AI tools that turn technical input into domain-specific output for experts, and MedVault's schema-constrained LLM pipeline is the closest AI build the candidate has.

leads.summary: Vendah runs a marketplace connecting beauty brands to individual resellers across Brazil, with embedded microcredit for sellers and a reseller site that sells kits and offers payment plans.
leads.hook: The posting says GMV is growing about 30% month over month, with approximately 1,000 active sellers and a proprietary credit engine.
leads.angle_reason: The marketplace needs user accounts and a credit engine on top, which maps to MedVault's Django backend, JWT auth and per-user data isolation.

leads.summary: Letterdrop sells go-to-market intelligence that surfaces which accounts are evaluating competitors and which buyers are in market, for sales and marketing teams.
leads.hook: A July post on the Letterdrop blog compared buying signals with real CRM data at four B2B companies to check whether they predict competitor deals.
leads.angle_reason: Letterdrop is a GenAI data product, and MedVault's LLM pipeline with schema-constrained output is the closest build the candidate has.

leads.summary: Magic Patterns is an AI design tool where product teams turn prompts, PRDs and repos into high-fidelity UI on a shared canvas, then hand the chosen direction to a coding agent.
leads.hook: The homepage says Magic OS takes in a PRD and repo, compares design directions side by side, and hands the winner to a coding agent.
leads.angle_reason: Magic Patterns ingests a repo and hands output to coding agents, and Canopy already reads GitHub repositories and maps their structure.

leads.summary: Narrative, now rebranded as Zorro, makes AI testing agents that run bug bashes and regression tests on pull requests, with plain-English tests that self-heal when the UI changes.
leads.hook: The site says Zorro runs AI regression tests on pull requests and auto-heals selector changes, with no test cases to maintain.
leads.angle_reason: Zorro runs checks on pull requests and integrates with coding agents, the same developer-tooling space as Canopy's repository analysis and CI-style checks.
